editorial:
Imagine getting a call from your dad saying he is turning ninety, but there is a huge catch: he plans to end his life the moment the party is over. That is exactly what the three adult children in this story have to deal with. You get a wild mix of family fighting, old secrets, and a very stubborn grandfather who refuses to go quietly into the night. The vibe is a bit like a family reunion from hell, but it has a lot of heart beneath all the arguing. It is a funny look at how people handle death and the messy relationships that stay with us until the end.

You will really love the acting here because the lead character is a total scene-stealer who keeps you guessing. The pacing is steady, though some of the family drama feels a bit slow in the middle. If you enjoy stories about dysfunctional families and dark humor, you should definitely give this a try. Since it is an older flick, you might want to look for a high-quality version to keep the picture crisp.
endingExplained: In the end, the father's plan to leave on his own terms forces his children to finally face their problems and bond as a family. After all the fighting and crying, they realize how much they actually love him. Instead of a tragic finish, the movie wraps up with a feeling of peace. He finds a reason to keep living a bit longer because he sees his kids have finally grown up and reconciled.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family dramas with a dark sense of humor.
